claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

  - Child is not in hospital or residential accommodation
  - Child is not fostered
  - Child does not work 24+ hours/week
  - Child has not started an apprenticeship in England
  - Child does not receive qualifying benefits in their own right

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit! Let me start the eligibility assessment process.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! Let me start with the first question:

**How old is the child you're claiming Child Benefit for?** 

Please tell me their age, and I'll help determine which eligibility pathway applies to them. Child Benefit has different rules depending on whether the child is:
- **Under 16 years old**
- **16-19 years old** (may need to be in education or training)
- **20 years old or over**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Oh, I'm asking about my son Alex. He's 3 years old.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! Thank you for that information. Your son Alex is 3 years old, which means he's under 16. Let me proceed with the next eligibility check.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! Now I need to ask you about Alex's work situation:

**Is Alex working less than 24 hours per week, or is he not in paid work at all?**

(Since Alex is only 3 years old, I expect the answer is that he's not in paid work, but I need to confirm this to proceed with the assessment.)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he's not working at all - he's only 3! He's just at home with me.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Excellent! That makes sense - at 3 years old, Alex is definitely not in paid work. Let me continue with the next check.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Now I need to check about benefits:

**Is Alex NOT receiving any of these benefits in his own name:**
- Employment and Support Allowance (ESA)
- Universal Credit

(At age 3, this would be very unlikely, but I need to confirm this for the assessment.)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he doesn't get any benefits in his own name. He's just a toddler.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! That's what I'd expect. Let me continue.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Now I need to check about apprenticeships:

**Is Alex in an apprenticeship?**

Given that Alex is only 3 years old, the answer should be no, but I need to confirm this to proceed.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, of course not - he's only 3 years old!

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Of course! That's perfectly clear. Let me move forward to the next check.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Now I need to check your residency status. This is an important requirement for Child Benefit. There are several possible paths that can qualify:

**Which of the following applies to you?**

1. **You normally live in the UK** - This is the most common situation
2. **You have settled status under the EU Settlement Scheme**
3. **You have pre-settled status under the EU Settlement Scheme AND:**
   - You're working and earning/expect to earn above the National Insurance threshold for 3 continuous months, OR
   - You're actively looking for work (jobseeker - up to 91 days), OR
   - You have sufficient resources to support your family (not claiming Income Support, income-based JSA, Pension Credit, or Universal Credit), OR
   - You're studying with sufficient resources, OR
   - You're a family member of an EEA or Swiss national
4. **You're a Crown servant living abroad** in certain qualifying countries

Which of these best describes your situation?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I live in the UK - I'm in Manchester with Alex.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Excellent! That's straightforward. You normally live in the UK in Manchester. Let me proceed to the next check.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Good! Now I need to check if you're responsible for Alex. "Responsibility" means one of the following:

**Which applies to you?**

1. **You live with Alex** - You share the same household
2. **You're contributing to Alex's upkeep** - You pay for things like food, clothes, pocket money, housing, or presents (at least the equivalent of the Child Benefit amount)
3. **You're paying maintenance** - You make payments towards Alex's maintenance under a court order or agreement

Based on what you've told me (that Alex is at home with you), I'd expect you live with him. Can you confirm?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, Alex lives at home with me in Manchester.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! That's clear - you live with Alex. Let me continue to the next check.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Now I need to check an important question about other potential claimants:

**Is anyone else (like Alex's other parent, a grandparent, or guardian) also claiming or planning to claim Child Benefit for Alex?**

This is important because only one person can claim Child Benefit for each child. If there are multiple potential claimants:
- If you've agreed who should claim, that's fine and we can proceed
- If there's a dispute about who should claim, HMRC will need to make the final decision

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, nobody else is claiming Child Benefit for Alex.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Great! That's clear - you're the only potential claimant for Alex. Let me proceed to the next check.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Now I need to check about Alex's living situation:

**Is Alex:**
1. **In hospital?**
2. **In care** (such as a care home or local authority care)?
3. **Fostered** (living with foster carers)?
4. **Living normally at home with you?**

Which applies to Alex?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: He's living normally at home with me.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! Alex is living normally at home with you. Let me continue.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Almost there! One final check:

**Is the local council NOT paying towards Alex's accommodation or maintenance?**

In other words, you're not receiving support from the council to pay for his housing or care - you're covering these costs yourself (or through other means like your own income).

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: That's right - the council isn't paying anything towards Alex. I'm taking care of him myself.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Excellent! That's all the information I need. You've met all the eligibility requirements for Child Benefit for Alex. Let me provide you with the final outcome.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
## ✅ **You Are Eligible for Child Benefit for Alex!**

Great news! Based on your circumstances, **you are eligible to claim Child Benefit for your 3-year-old son Alex**.

### Summary of Your Eligibility:

You meet all the key requirements:
- ✅ Alex is a qualifying child (under 16 years old)
- ✅ He is not working or receiving benefits in his own right
- ✅ You live with Alex in the UK (Manchester)
- ✅ You are responsible for his care and upkeep
- ✅ No one else is claiming for him
- ✅ The local council is not paying towards his care

### Next Steps:

To claim Child Benefit, you'll need to:
1. Apply through the official government website or contact HMRC
2. Have the following information ready:
   - Your National Insurance number
   - Alex's full name and date of birth
   - Details of any other children you're claiming for
   - Bank account details for payment

For more information and to make your claim, visit: **https://www.gov.uk/child-benefit**

If you have any other children you'd like me to check eligibility for, just let me know their details and I can help with those too!
